summary: This step starts Track 2 from the child's two BUB1B alleles and the BubR1 protein instead of from drug databases, and runs four routes, each gated by its own positive control. R1 (entry 158) reads the stop allele: a UGA stop with a +4 A in exon 17 of 23, 746 nt before the last exon junction, so the message is destroyed by NMD and the kinase domain is lost. A readthrough model over 5,837 measured stops passes its held-out control for DAP, G418 and SRI-41315 while the no-drug column fails as it must; but even a perfect readthrough agent adds at most 1.42 points of working BubR1 against a gap of about 6.5, so the missense allele is the lever. R2 (entry 159) reads protein-level drug data: the HSP90 to HSPA1A control ranks 1 and 2 of 875; BUB1B protein is one of the most proliferation-bound proteins measured (99.7th percentile); after correction five approved drugs raise it by only 14 to 16 per cent, the strongest raisers (a CDK1 inhibitor and a proteasome inhibitor) point at degradation, and the cell-cycle-corrected LINCS control fails, leaving TTK as the one checkpoint gene whose knockout still resembles BUB1B's. R3 (entry 160) reads the literature with a code-checked quote gate: unseeded queries recover all three landmark papers, 42 of 42 quotes verify, and the rows name NAD+ precursors, HDAC inhibitors, proteasome inhibitors, hypomethylating agents and senolytics, plus safety evidence from MVA patients themselves: a severe dactinomycin reaction, a published warning against vincristine and taxol, and growth hormone ineffective in four reports. R4 (entry 161) does not add a route: it weighs R1-R3's 50 rows (45 drugs after dedup and class expansion) against the two unmeasured facts, under a per-child safety factor and a 35-row avoid list. The best action now is gliclazide tied with migalastat (EU 0.385), and it is not robust - three assumptions move it. What is robust is the price of the next measurement: EVPI 0.180, all of it on whether the missense protein is unstable or inactive, nothing on readthrough, and a cycloheximide-chase blot captures 0.106 of it, 59 %, positive over every range swept. The transfer check (entry 162) then re-ran R1-R3 on Bloom syndrome: three case cards (587 configuration lines) plus 271 lines of shared-code parameterisation against entry 156's 378-line purpose-built driver, all nine first-case tables byte-identical, R2 needing no card at all - and R3's declared control failing (retrieval 3/3, extraction 0/3), so its five BLM rows are reported as uninterpretable.
why: Iterations 2 and 4 asked drug databases and screens first; their generators came back refuted or at chance (entries 142, 153, 154, 155), and the leads that survived came from mechanism and papers (entry 150). The user chose an exploratory step with no pre-registered claims; a positive control per route replaces pre-registration (docs/iteration5/notes/exploratory-no-hypotheses.md).
verdict: Outcome, not a verdict: no claims were filed. Four of six declared controls passed and their routes ran (R1 for three compounds only, R2 in the primary proteome dataset, R3 in both halves, R4's hand-worked case reproduced exactly); two failed - R2's cell-cycle-corrected LINCS reversal and R3 on the transfer case - and both are reported as uninterpretable rather than argued around. Across routes the answer points one way: the stop allele is not worth treating, the missense allele is, and which drug class fits depends on whether the missense protein is unstable or inactive, which no data here decides. R4 prices that gap instead of guessing it - the cycloheximide-chase blot is worth 59 % of perfect knowledge while the top-ranked drug flips under three separate assumptions, so the step's deliverable is a measurement and an avoid list, not a prescription. The transfer check shows the three routes move to a second disease by case card, at roughly a third of iteration 4's per-case cost, with one residual case-shaped leak left standing and recorded.

inherits.what: No step inside iteration 5. From iteration 4, reused as is: the mechanism card, the phenotype twin (entry 150), the per-child safety method (entries 152 and 155), the BUB1B stability atlas and published alleles (entry 149), and the normalized allele records (entry 114). The confirmed BUB1B pair comes from Track 1's oracle reply (entry 083).

hands_to.what: The candidate tables ressources/track2/it5/{readthrough,protein,literature}_candidates.tsv, in one shared schema with a branch column, to R4's decision analysis; R4's ressources/track2/it5/decision_{utilities,states,voi,flips,sweep,tornado,avoid}.tsv and decision_summary.json, plus the transfer tables under ressources/track2/it5/transfer/, to submissions/track2/iteration-5/.

figures.name: r1-stop-anatomy.svg
figures.reads: The BUB1B transcript's 23 exons in transcript order: the exons before the stop, the exon carrying it (17), and the exons the truncated protein never reaches; the stop sits 746 nt upstream of the last exon-exon junction, far past the 50-55 nt rule. The kinase domain lies entirely in the lost part.
figures.means: The stop allele's message is NMD-competent and would encode a protein without its kinase domain, so it contributes essentially no working BubR1.

figures.name: r1-control.svg
figures.reads: Spearman rho and pairwise ordering accuracy per compound on two held-out sets (14 named benchmark stops; a random fifth of 5,781), against the bar fixed before the run (rho 0.5, ordering 0.7). DAP, G418 and SRI-41315 clear it on both; five compounds fail one; the untreated column scores rho 0.02 and 0.12.
figures.means: The context model is interpretable for three compounds and for nothing else, and the no-drug negative control shows it is not fitting assay structure.

figures.name: r1-plus4.svg
figures.reads: Predicted readthrough for a UGA stop per compound under each of the four +4 bases, with the child's actual base (A) marked and the no-drug floor dotted. Moving A to C raises G418 3.6-fold but DAP only 1.3-fold; gentamicin sits 18 per cent above the floor.
figures.means: For this child's stop, context rather than potency ranks the drugs: UGA-selective agents keep their effect and aminoglycosides do not.

figures.name: r1-dosage.svg
figures.reads: Working BubR1 as a percent of wild type per scenario (untreated states, treatments) against published genotypes as yardsticks. The base case is 12.5 per cent; readthrough adds 0.01 to 0.07 points, a perfect readthrough agent 1.42, a 2-fold stabilisation of the missense protein 12.5.
figures.means: Readthrough cannot close the roughly 6.5-point gap even at its ceiling; stabilising the missense protein could, so the missense allele is the lever.

figures.name: r2-proliferation.svg
figures.reads: Left: BUB1B protein log2 fold change against the proliferation score for 875 compounds, with the fitted line (r 0.925). Right: the same compounds by corrected rank, 18 above the z 3 cut with the protein up.
figures.means: Most of what a drug does to BubR1 protein is a change in how many cells divide; only the residual can be read as a raise.

figures.name: r2-control.svg
figures.reads: (a) Gating-control ranks: HSPA1A under the two HSP90 inhibitors ranks 1 and 2 of 875 in Mitchell 2023; MDM2 under nutlin falls outside the cut in two ProTargetMiner sets. (b) LINCS checkpoint-sibling percentiles uncorrected and corrected: TTK stays rank 1, BUB1 moves from the 9th to the 88th percentile.
figures.means: The proteome route can see a real protein induction, so its BUB1B hits may be read; the corrected LINCS route cannot pass its control, so no reverser list exists.

figures.name: r2-hits.svg
figures.reads: Robust z of the corrected residual against raw BUB1B log2 fold change for 875 compounds, marker size by breadth: five approved corrected risers at +14 to +16 per cent, Ro-3306 (+88 per cent) and epoxomicin as broad non-approved risers, nutlins at high z with the protein down.
figures.means: No approved drug raises BubR1 protein by much, and the largest raises come from holding cells before mitosis or blocking degradation, which points at degradation as the lever for an unstable missense protein.

figures.name: r3-extraction-funnel.svg
figures.reads: Log-scale funnel of the intervention half: 767 papers retrieved, 760 with a cached text, 1,065 texts, 1,109 sentences past the screen, 30 rows written, 30 past the quote gate, 24 approved-drug candidate rows. The exposure half (12 rows, all verified) is drawn separately.
figures.means: Every row that reaches a candidate carries a sentence code found verbatim in the cached source; the screen, not the gate, is the recall bottleneck.

figures.name: r3-evidence-map.svg
figures.reads: Interventions against the effect they had (BubR1 level, acetylation, aneuploidy, senescence, lifespan, tumours), one square per verified row, coloured by whether the direction is the one a hypomorph wants, sized by model (animal or patient vs cells).
figures.means: The literature holds seven distinct ways to raise BubR1 protein and several downstream rescues that no drug database encodes; most act on stability or transcription.

figures.name: r3-mva-exposures.svg
figures.reads: What MVA patients in case reports were given and how it went: dactinomycin with a severe reaction, a warning against vincristine and taxol, treosulfan conditioning tolerated then graft rejection and death, growth hormone without response in four reports.
figures.means: The disease's own record gives specific safety evidence for this child: antimitotic chemotherapy and growth hormone need caution, and the rhabdomyosarcoma term makes the vincristine warning directly relevant.

figures.name: r4-decision-tree.svg
figures.reads: The two unmeasured facts as a tree: missense_class (unstable 0.55 / inactive 0.45) branching into readthrough_feasible (yes 0.00 / no 1.00), each of the four leaves ending in the best action for that world-state and its heuristic utility - gliclazide tied with migalastat at 0.70 where the missense is unstable, dasatinib at 0.40 where it is inactive.
figures.means: The choice is decided entirely by the missense question; the readthrough branch carries no prior weight and changes no leaf, so the decision has one real fork, not four.
figures.source: tools/render_it5_r4.py over ressources/track2/it5/decision_states.tsv and decision_summary.json; entry 161

figures.name: r4-voi-curve.svg
figures.reads: EVPI and the EVSI of each named test plotted against each prior as it is swept from 0 to 1, with the exact flip point marked and each segment labelled by the action that is best there. At the configured prior of 0.55, EVPI is 0.180 and the cycloheximide-chase blot's EVSI is 0.106; the readthrough reporter assay lies flat at 0.
figures.means: A named bench test is worth 59 % of everything perfect knowledge could buy, and the second test is worth nothing - so the step's recommendation is one measurement, not a ranked list.
figures.source: tools/render_it5_r4.py over ressources/track2/it5/decision_voi.tsv, decision_sweep.tsv and decision_flips.tsv; entry 161

figures.name: r4-heatmap.svg
figures.reads: The top 15 actions by expected utility against the four world-states, each cell shaded by heuristic utility and the best action in each state outlined; every row label carries the drug's per-child safety class, and 24 of the 45 drugs are unassessed.
figures.means: Most candidates are flat across the states - they are `any`-branch rows that no measurement would move - and the few that are not are exactly the rows the blot would separate; the safety labels show how thin the assessment behind any of them is.

figures.name: r4-tornado.svg
figures.reads: One bar per configured parameter, showing the blot's EVSI as that parameter alone runs from its low to its high value with the rest held, longest bar on top: blot sensitivity 0.6 to 0.99 moves it 0.028 to 0.150, and the whole sweep stays inside 0.005 to 0.150. Three bars are marked as changing the recommended drug - P(unstable) 0.2, R2 route weight 0.25, and unassessed drugs given full weight.
figures.means: The asymmetry that is the step's main result: the recommended drug is not robust to three separate assumptions, while the value of running the blot is positive under every one of them.

figures.name: s1-transfer.svg
figures.reads: What moving each of R1, R2 and R3 to Bloom syndrome cost: configuration lines in a new case card against lines of shared-code change, with the new capability shown separately, the control verdict per route, and entry 156's 378-line purpose-built driver drawn as the yardstick. R1 311 config lines, R2 none at all, R3 276; 587 configuration and 271 parameterisation lines in total.
figures.means: The three routes transfer by case card rather than by a new driver, at roughly a third of iteration 4's per-case cost - but 'configuration only' was still false as they stood, and R3's control failed on the second case, so the claim is reported with both numbers against it.
